Excellent work, everyone. Daniel's framing is exactly right — we present this as a single coordinated package to Northlake rather than piecemeal requests. Let me synthesize where we stand so we're all aligned before I draft the renegotiation communication.

We have four items for the package:

1. Royalty reduction: Sofia's benchmark supports a 2.25% ceiling, so we push to bring the 3% rate down to at or below 2.25%.

2. Title cure: Daniel has identified a missing inventor assignment on the continuation application. Northlake must obtain and record that assignment before signing — this is a condition precedent, not a post-closing obligation, given that the business team wants immediate access post-execution.

3. Export-control provisions: Nora's ECCN 3A001 classification requires two license clauses — a prohibition on transfers to military end users and an annual end-use screening certification. We also need Nora's recommendation on whether early-access diligence triggers deemed export concerns with non-U.S. persons, and if so, we condition early access accordingly.

4. Pre-existing rights carveout: Martin's discovery of the University Research Consortium grant means our exclusive license must explicitly reserve those academic research and teaching uses.

Before I draft the package, I have two questions. Nora, can you confirm by when you can assess the deemed export risk for the early-access period? And Martin, is there anything in the prior grant language that suggests Northlake's consortium grant could extend beyond academic research and teaching into commercial applications? That would affect how narrowly we draw the carveout.
